title.narrative: Ukraine Crisis 2022 - WFP Ukraine Limited Emergency Operation 2022

description.narrative:
Aktuell insats avser Sidas bidrag av medel till FN:s livsmedelsprogram (WFP) med anledning av akut livsmedelsotrygghet i länder såsom Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Centralafrikanska republiken, Demokratiska republiken Kongo, El Salvador, Etiopien, Guatemala, Guinea, Haiti, Honduras, Jemen, Kamerun, Kenya, Kuba, Madagaskar, Mali, Mauretanien, Moçambique, Myanmar, Niger, Nigeria, Palestina, Somalia, Sudan, Sydsudan, Syrien, Tchad, Uganda, Ukraina, Venezuela och Zambia.
Stödet omfattar totalt 2 307 500 000 kronor under avtalsperioden, inklusive 257 000 000 kronor för att nå krisdrabbade människor i 12 länder under år 2026.
Insatsen innefattar även stöd till FN:s humanitära flygtjänst (UNHAS) i syfte att möjliggöra tillträde för humanitära aktörer till människor i behov av humanitärt stöd i områden som inte är tillgängliga genom andra lösningar.

The current contribution provides Sida funding to the World Food Programme (WFP) to support the organisation’s humanitarian response to acute food insecurity in countries such as Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Cuba, Democratic Republic of the Congo, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Guinea, Haiti, Honduras, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Myanmar, Niger, Nigeria, Palestine, Somalia, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine, Venezuela and Zambia.
The support amounts to a total of SEK 2,307,500,000 over the agreement period, including SEK 257,000,000 to reach crisis-affected populations in 12 countries in 2026.
The intervention also includes support to the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) to facilitate access for humanitarian actors to people in need of assistance in areas that cannot be reached by other means.

WFPs impact-level indicators encompasses SDG Goal 2: Support countries in achieving Zero Hunger and SDG Goal 17: Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development. WFP cross-cutting priorities are "Protection and accountability to affected populations", "Gender equality and womens empowerment", "Environmental sustainability" and "Nutrition integration".
The partners programme results are accordingly formulated based on five strategic outcomes:
Outcome 1: People are better able to meet their urgent food and nutrition needs
1.1 People have access to nutritious food, cash, assets and services in emergencies.
1.2 People and communities have the awareness, knowledge, skills, motivation and practices to consume a healthy diet and improve nutrition outcomes for those most vulnerable.
1.3 Increased enrolment in and adherence to malnutrition prevention programmes.
1.4 Increase in number of nutrition vulnerable individuals treated for wasting.
1.5 People have sufficient access to nutritious food, cash, other assets and services before a shock hits.
1.6 People have sufficient access to services, food and cash transfers to protect their livelihoods at the onset of an emergency.
1.7 Girls and boys have increased access to school, health and nutrition packages in emergencies.
1.8 Social and public-sector institutions have enhanced capacity to assist populations facing acute food insecurity and malnutrition.
1.9 WFP responses complement national social protection, where appropriate.
1.10 WFP technical support for social protection system architecture, programmes and knowledge.
1.11 People have increased access to and availability of nutritious foods for a healthy die.
Outcome 2: People have better nutrition, health and education outcomes
2.1 People have access to nutritious food, cash, assets and services in non-emergencies.
2.2 People and communities have the awareness, knowledge, skills, motivation and practices to consume a healthy diet and improve nutrition outcomes for those most vulnerable.
2.3 Increased enrolment in and adherence to malnutrition prevention programmes.
2.4 Increase in number of nutrition vulnerable individuals treated for wasting.
2.5 People have increased awareness of the benefits of school health and nutrition packages.
2.6 Girls and boys have increased access to school, health and nutrition packages.
2.7 National social and public-sector institutions have enhanced capacity to address chronic hunger and malnutrition.
2.8 WFP responses complement national social protection, where appropriate.
2.9 WFP technical support for social protection system architecture, programmes and knowledge provided.
2.10 People have increased access to and availability of nutritious foods for a healthy diet.
Outcome 3: People have improved and sustainable livelihoods
3.1 People and communities have increased livelihood skills, capacities and access to financial services and energy products for climate adapted and sustainable livelihoods.
3.2 People and communities have improved access to productive assets.
3.3 Smallholder farmers have increased capacities to produce and aggregate marketable surplus and reduce post-harvest losses, and access markets and energy products.
3.4 Improved linkages between local food suppliers and buyers, including schools and other institutional buyers, private sector and WFP.
3.5 National actors have enhanced capacity to promote sustainable livelihoods, strengthen local value chains, and protect communities against shocks.
3.6 WFP responses complement national social protection, where appropriate.
3.7 WFP technical support for social protection system architecture, programmes and knowledge provided.
3.8 People and communities have access to and availability to of nutritious food and/or awareness, knowledge, skills, motivation and practices to consume a healthy diet and improve nutrition outcomes for those most vulnerable.
Outcome 4: National programmes and systems are strengthened
4.1 The prominence of national policies, institutions and programmes contributing to zero hunger is enhanced through advocacy and dialogue.
4.2 National actors make evidence-based decisions to achieve Zero Hunger, supported through provision of WFP knowledge products.
4.3 National institutions improve institutional and programmatic processes to achieve SDGs supported by WFP technical advice.
4.4 National organizations have access to improved equipment and assets to support their activities.
4.5 National actors have improved technical, functional and soft skills with WFP training and coaching support.
4.6 National actors have captured and shared southern solutions contributing to zero hunger by engaging in WFP-facilitated South-South and triangular cooperation.
4.7 WFP technical support for social protection system architecture, programmes and knowledge provided.
Outcome 5: Humanitarian and development actors are more efficient & effective
5.1. Governments, humanitarian and development actors utilise on-demand and mandated services to effectively set-up, manage and deliver.
